newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 22.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Wednesday:
* Chrysler Corp's fourth-quarter earnings exceeded Wall Street expectations and gave the company its second-most-profitable year ever.
* Allied Irish Banks Plc agreed to acquire Pennsylvania's Dauphin Deposit Corp for $1.36 billion.
* Chase Manhattan Corp and Citicorp reported small increases in fourth-quarter profits.
* Boeing Co's stock rose after the company decided not to pursue a mulitbillion dollar plan to make larger 747 jets.
* Salomon Inc net income nearly doubled in 1996 on revenues from trading and investment banking.
* Exxon Corp's fourth-quarter profits surged nearly 49 percent, and earnings of Shell Oil Co, a unit of Royal Dutch/Shell Group, jumped 51 percent.
* Pacific Telesis Group, SBC Communications Inc, NYNEX Corp and Bell Atlantic Corp reported generally healthy profits.
* Stock prices surged on strong earnings reports and on positive remarks from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
* Inflation-indexed bonds began trading at high prices and low yields.
* Intel Corp plans to incorporate offbeat humor in a new campaign by its advertising agency, which is a unit of Havas Advertising.
* New York Times Co will introduce new business pages in its Metropolitan section.
* Microsoft Corp is tapping into Manhattan's Silicon Alley to develop new projects with on-line media companies in New York, including an on-line show and a documentary series.
* Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said that the economy shows few signs of inflationary tensions, but hints that larger wage increases may be starting to fuel rising prices.
* In the next four years, at least 17 Japanese and European car makers plan to introduce new sport utility vehicles to tap a market dominated by American auto makers.
* New York Times Co will begin changes next month to expand its national distribution.
* International Business Machines Corp fourth quarter earnings exceed forecasts, but some analysts fear the results are not enough to sustain the company's momentum.
